To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary and hormonal factors may affect the tumor microenvironment by altering IL-1Ra, IL-1β, and angiogenesis.
tamoxifen, Flx, and ENL increase stroma- but not cancer cell-derived IL1Ra and decrease angiogenesis in estrogen-sensitive breast cancers.

dietary interventions with tamoxifen, fl axseed, and the mammalian-derived lignan enterolac tone, but not the plant-derived phytoestrogen genistein, increased the IL-1Ra/ IL-1β ratio in the tumor microenvironment and in tumor cells in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of proinflammatory cytokine signaling in breast cancer.
the role of the pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, IL-1α, IL-1β, and IL-1Ra, in breast cancer development.

the development of novel antiestrogens for the treatment of breast cancer, with special focus on the effects of phytoestrogenic compounds, such as the lignans in Flax and the isoflavones in GEN, on breast cancer growth and progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

dietary phytoestrogents and the antiestrogenic drug tamoxifen, in addition to the previously described effects on cancer cell growth, may decrease breast cancer progression by inhibiting angiogenesis through increased release of IL- 1Ra from both the stroma and cancer cells.

the release of the IL-1s from both cancer cells and the tumor stroma, where the macrophages are an important component, may represent a feasible target for antiestrogen treatment and dietary intervention against breast cancer.
dietary Flaxseed and ENL, and tamoxifen, but not GEN, may affect tumor growth by decreasing the proangiogenic cytokine IL-1β, and increasing the antiangiogenic cytokine receptor antagonist, IL-1RA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tamoxifen, Flavseed, and ENL may decrease IL-1β release from the murine tumor stroma, thereby decreasing breast cancer angiogenesis, and that the antiestrogenic effects of these agents may be mediated through the release of IL-Ra.
the antiestrogenic properties of tamoxifen and the lignans in Flax and ENL may be mediated via IL-1β and IL-1Ra in the breast cancer microenvironment.
tamoxifen, Flx, and ENL, but not GEN, increase IL-1Ra, decrease IL-1β and tumor angiogenesis, and decrease breast cancer growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor microenvironment may serve as a target for anti-estrogen therapy and that dietary interventions, such as the intake of Flax and ENL, may be beneficial.
the antiestrogenic effects of tamoxifen, Flav and ENL on breast cancer may involve the release of IL1Ra and the inhibition of IL1β-induced tumor angiogenesis.
the tumor microenvironment is important for breast cancer progression and may be a target for antiestrogens and phytoestrogene-rich foods.
